title: ML platform lead at an inference startup

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Thanks for making time today. To start, can you walk me through how you serve models right now?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.text: Sure. We run a chat product on about four hundred H100s, mostly serving a seventy billion parameter model with vLLM.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Got it. Where does that setup start to struggle?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.text: Long context is the big one. Once conversations pass about a hundred thousand tokens the KV cache blows past GPU memory and we start evicting, so latency spikes.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: How are you handling that today?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.text: Honestly we've been buying more H200s mostly for the extra HBM, which is painful because we don't need the compute.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Makes sense. Is solving this tied to any timeline on your side?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.text: We want something in production before our enterprise launch at the end of Q2, so a pilot would need to start next month.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: And who besides you would weigh in on a decision like this?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.text: Our CTO signs off on anything over fifty thousand dollars, and the infra team would run the pilot.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Helpful. One concern people raise with CXL is latency. Is that on your mind?

turns.speaker: prospect
turns.text: Yeah, if pooled memory adds more than a few microseconds per token, the whole thing is dead on arrival for us.
